**QLoRA combines a compressed frozen base with small trainable adapters.** The large pretrained weights are stored in a low-bit representation, while LoRA parameters learn the task-specific update. Computation uses suitable higher-precision representations where needed. This saves memory mainly by avoiding full-precision storage and optimizer states for a fully trainable base. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314)

**NF4 is a quantization codebook choice.** NormalFloat4 allocates representable values in a way motivated by approximately normally distributed weights. It is not the same as simply rounding every weight to one of 16 uniformly spaced numbers. Real weight distributions and block scaling still affect quantization error.

**Double quantization compresses the metadata too.** Blockwise quantization stores scales or related constants for many groups. Quantizing those constants reduces their additional memory footprint. The saving comes from a second layer of compression, not from applying the same rounding step twice to each weight.

Paged optimizers use memory-management mechanisms to handle optimizer-state pressure and transient memory spikes. Moving data between memory tiers can avoid out-of-memory failures but can also add transfer overhead; it is not free GPU memory.

**Know what remains expensive.** Activations, LoRA gradients/states, temporary dequantized values, and attention caches still consume memory. The base weights are frozen, but gradients may still propagate through their computations to train adapters. Validate quality against an appropriate higher-precision baseline and use supported kernels; a small stored model is not automatically a fast training configuration.

**Technical details and references.**

QLoRA stores a frozen base model in 4-bit quantized form while training small higher-precision LoRA updates. During computation, needed base blocks are dequantized into a compute dtype; gradients update adapters, not the discrete base codes. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314)

NF4 uses nonuniform levels designed around a normal weight distribution. Double quantization compresses the block-scale metadata as well as weights. Paged optimizers use managed memory to accommodate optimizer-memory spikes, with potential transfer overhead.

$$W_{effective}=\operatorname{dequant}(W_{4bit})+sBA.$$

Four-bit storage does not mean every multiplication or activation is four-bit. Include quantization metadata, adapters, gradients, optimizer states, activations, and temporary dequantized tiles in capacity estimates. Calibration/quantization choices and adapter capacity still affect quality; QLoRA is parameter-efficient fine-tuning, not unrestricted full-parameter training at four bits.
